final_message:
DONE

I've built the catch-up plan workbook and a short email draft to send with it. I checked every formula with a separate calculation tool (pycel), and the results match my own week-by-week model.

**Recommended plan:**
- **Weeks 4–12 – stay on 6 days.** At 180 hrs/week the past-due hours are gone by week 9. But week 10 needs 221 hrs, which puts you about 23 hrs behind again. From week 11 you stay caught up, and by the end of week 12 you have about 86 hrs of buffer (about 2.9 days). So building the buffer takes 9 weeks on 6 days.
- **Weeks 13–14 – 5 days.** Week 13 needs 189 hrs, more than 5-day capacity, and the buffer covers the difference.
- **Week 15 onward – regular 4-day weeks.** The buffer never drops below the 30-hr (one day) minimum, and the plan's rule check finds no weeks that break it. Overtime falls from 98 to 20 OT days per person through week 52.

**Cutting days early without less demand:** each day dropped adds 30 hrs/week to the backlog.

| Option | Caught up by | Peak past due |
|---|---|---|
| Recommended | Week 11 | 259 hrs (week 4) |
| 5 days from week 4 | Week 19 | 308 hrs |
| 4 days from week 4 | Week 26 | 544 hrs |
| 4 days as soon as backlog first clears (week 10) | Week 20 | Back to 184 hrs behind |

**Assumptions to check (also written into the workbook):**
- The `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders were empty, so there was no registry of operative records. The plan is based only on the reference workbook.
- That workbook only has demand figures, so I calculated capacity and balances from 30 hrs/day.
- The 30-hr minimum buffer is my own planning choice, and it's a close call: switching to 4 days in week 14 instead would miss it by less than 0.1 hr.
- Building a buffer assumes work can be done ahead of its scheduled week, meaning orders are released and material is available.
- Team size and labour rates weren't given, so overtime is shown per person, not as total hours or cost.
- Demand after about week 18 looks low, probably because those orders haven't been released yet. The later buffer figures are optimistic, and the plan should be re-run every week.

The workbook uses live formulas, so you can change the days or the buffer target and everything updates. Values will show when it's opened in Excel, but tools that read the file without calculating it will see blank cells.

Files in `outputs/`:
- `MIG_Weld_CatchUp_Plan.xlsx` – summary, inputs, weekly plan, scenario comparison with chart, and a copy of the source data
- `Email_Summary_to_Manager.docx`
